flags.headline: NVDA -5.08% on $250B Ohio data-center financing-guarantee report; part of a global AI-chip rout
flags.detail: NVDA fell from $207.07 to $196.56 after the WSJ reported Nvidia is in talks to guarantee financing for a $250B, 10-gigawatt data-center project in Ohio, reviving investor concern about 'circular AI financing' — Nvidia funding the demand for its own chips — and whether AI capex reflects genuine end demand. This lands inside a broader, severe global chip selloff (Bloomberg: worst day for the sector since April 2025) triggered by a Shanghai state-backed firm reportedly mass-producing homegrown DUV lithography machines, a category ASML has dominated — reviving China-domestic-capability competition fears across the whole semiconductor supply chain. Samsung -13.4%, SK Hynix -14.7% (KOSPI -10.8%, its worst day in decades), Kioxia -18.3%, MediaTek -10%. Lands 1-2 sessions ahead of MSFT/META (7/29) and AMZN/GOOGL (7/30-31) hyperscaler capex commentary.
flags.thesis_link: No direct match to a listed NVDA key_risk — the vendor-financing/circular-financing structure is a new risk vector not previously captured in the screener thesis (existing risks cover capex-sustainability and custom-ASIC competition, not NVDA acting as a financing guarantor). Flagging as RED on materiality (global, tier-1-sourced, sector-wide selloff) and recommend the next screener refresh add a vendor-financing-concentration risk line.

evidence.source: Bloomberg — Chip Rout Deepens on China Competition, Circular Funding Fears
The Motley Fool — Why Nvidia Stock Fell Today

flags.headline: Risk Sentinel's Dashboard sync silently failed for ~26 of the last 30 sessions — real analysis existed, the desk never saw it
flags.detail: Investigating this run's Step 0 turned up a real daily risk-monitor.json on an orphaned claude/gifted-einstein-* branch in Stock-Screener for nearly every session from 2026-06-28 through 2026-07-27 (all but 2026-07-15) — the routine WAS running daily. But risk/ was never merged into Stock-Screener main (Step 9 only ever committed to the ephemeral run branch), and Step 0's recovery script picked a branch alphabetically rather than by recency, so each new session pulled an essentially random stale snapshot instead of the prior day's. Only 2026-06-28/29/30 and 2026-07-27 ever reached the Dashboard; yesterday's report went further and incorrectly told the desk there had been a '27-day monitoring gap' since 6/30, when in fact ~26 real runs existed and simply never surfaced. Recovered all available daily summaries into a corrected risk/risk-history.json (now 30 entries, 2026-06-28 to today, one genuine gap on 2026-07-15). Fixed both root causes today: RISK SENTINEL PROMPT.md Step 0 now ranks recovery candidates by commit date, and Step 9 now requires merging risk/ into Stock-Screener main every run (matching how daily-screening and opportunity-finder already handle reports/), so main — not scattered branches — is always the source of truth.
